verses.text: So, my brothers and sisters, whom I love and long for, my joy and my crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, dear friends!
I beg Euodia and I beg Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord.
Yes, and I ask you too, my true partner, to help these women. They worked hard with me to spread the Good News, along with Clement and my other co-workers. Their names are in the book of life.
Always be glad in the Lord. I will say it again: be glad!
Let everyone see how gentle you are. The Lord is near.
Do not worry about anything. Instead, in every situation, pray and ask God, and thank him, and tell him what you need.
Then God's peace, which is greater than we can understand, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers and sisters, think about whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, and whatever is worth admiring. If anything is excellent or worthy of praise, think about such things.
Keep doing what you have learnt and received from me, and what you heard from me and saw in me. And the God of peace will be with you.
I am very glad in the Lord that at last you have shown your care for me again. You did care, but you had no chance to show it.
I am not saying this because I am in need. I have learnt to be content whatever my situation.

I know what it is to have little, and I know what it is to have plenty. I have learnt the secret of being content in any and every situation, whether well fed or hungry, whether I have plenty or not enough.
I can do all this through Christ, who gives me strength.
Yet it was good of you to share in my troubles.
And you Philippians know this. In the early days of the Good News, when I left Macedonia, not one church shared with me in giving and receiving, except you.
Even when I was in Thessalonica, you sent me help more than once when I was in need.
It is not that I want your gift. I want more fruit to be added to your account.

I have received everything in full, and even more. I am well supplied, now that Epaphroditus has brought me the gifts you sent. They are a sweet-smelling offering, a sacrifice that God accepts and is pleased with.
And my God will meet all your needs from his glorious riches in Christ Jesus.
Glory to our God and Father for ever and ever. Amen.
Greet all God's people in Christ Jesus. The brothers and sisters with me send greetings.
All God's people here send you greetings, especially those in Caesar's household.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
